questions.name: Maturity Stage
questions.title: How would you describe where your L&D function is today?
questions.supporting_text: This tells us in 10 seconds whether we're talking to a CLO building from scratch, a mature team looking to scale, or someone drowning in legacy content.

answers.text: We're building our L&D function; most training is ad-hoc or informal.
We have some programs in place, but they're inconsistent or outdated.
We have established programs and an LMS, but we're stretched thin on capacity.
We have a mature L&D operation and need a strategic partner to level it up.
We're going through a major change (merger, growth, new system) that's resetting our L&D priorities.

questions.name: Business Pain Points
questions.title: What is your single biggest L&D challenge right now?
questions.supporting_text: This surfaces the immediate pain that brought you here and helps pinpoint where we need to focus first.

answers.text: Getting new hires productive faster and more consistently.
Keeping up with mandatory training and complex regulatory requirements.
Upskilling the team fast enough as the business or technology changes.
Modernising old classroom or PDF content for digital or remote delivery.
Launching a new LMS or learning platform and getting our people to actually use it.

questions.name: Delivery Models
questions.title: How is your training currently being delivered?
questions.supporting_text: This reveals the reality of your current learning ecosystem and helps identify structural gaps.

answers.text: Instructor-led training (ILT) - primarily classroom or in-person sessions.
Virtual instructor-led (VILT) - live, synchronous online sessions.
eLearning modules - structured SCORM/xAPI courses hosted on an LMS.
Microlearning - short videos, job aids, and quick-reference tools in the flow of work.
On-the-job training, peer mentoring, or unstructured self-directed learning.

questions.name: Team Capacity
questions.title: Tell us about your internal L&D team and how you currently get work done.
questions.supporting_text: A team of one building for 10,000 employees is a very different conversation from a large team that just needs specialized external skills.

answers.text: Just me, I wear many hats and handle everything end-to-end.
A small, agile team (2-5 people) managing multiple priorities.
A mid-size team (6-15 people) with some specialized roles.
A large team (15+ people) with dedicated instructional designers and administrators.
Mostly outsourced; we rely on external vendors to do the heavy lifting.

questions.name: Business Goals
questions.title: If you look back a year from now, what does great look like for your L&D function?
questions.supporting_text: This shifts the focus from "what do you need now" to "what are you trying to become," framing the ultimate goal of our assessment.

answers.text: Our people are trained faster and more consistently than they are today.
We've moved from classroom to digital, and our workforce actively engages with it.
We have a reliable partner doing the heavy lifting so our internal team can focus on strategy.
Our training is directly and measurably improving business performance.
Our L&D function has a seat at the leadership table and is viewed as a key driver of strategic growth.
